actual_question: What components and resource does the standard two-player Rival start with, what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card, and can its 10 VP trigger Endgame and victory?

fixed_key.expected_answer: Four cubes at Influence bottoms, three garrison troops rest supply, two Agents supply and third beside board, three Spies and one water supply, score/Combat zero. Retain Reshuffle in Hagal. Scoring Rival can trigger end at 10+ and win.
fixed_key.novelty: Rival full setup and scoring threat

requested_part_reasoning.requested: Identify the Rival’s starting physical components, quantities and starting water.
material_facts: twelve troops, with three in garrison and nine remaining in supply
three Agents, with two initially available in supply and the third/Swordmaster beside the board
Score and Combat markers initially at zero
requested_part_reasoning.scope_reasoning: The wording asks what components and resource it starts with. It does not expressly ask for every starting location or the complete setup procedure. Counts and the distinctions between initial troops/Agents and reserves are material to identifying its starting position. Merely saying four Influence cubes already identifies their type and quantity; stating their exact track positions is useful setup detail but not a separately requested material procedure. Likewise the question does not independently demand stating that the three Spies and water are physically in supply.

requested_part_reasoning.requested: State what happens to the 2P Reshuffle card.
material_facts: retain/keep it in the House Hagal deck rather than removing it

requested_part_reasoning.requested: State whether the standard Rival can trigger Endgame with 10 VP and can win.
material_facts: yes, its score of ten or more triggers Endgame
requested_part_reasoning.scope_reasoning: The question asks whether both outcomes are possible. A full replay of Endgame Intrigue, tiebreakers or final-scoring procedure is not required. Reaching ten does not itself guarantee victory; neither response claims that it does.

unasked_contextual_key_details.detail: Influence cubes specifically at the bottom of the tracks; Spies and starting water physically in supply.
unasked_contextual_key_details.reason: Helpful exact layout detail; the question asks which starting components/resource and asks two specific rule questions, rather than requesting all setup placements. A’s type/quantity statements meet the component identification request without these additional locators.

other_unasked_contextual_details: Selection of the Rival card, Ornithopter Objective assignment, human Objective assignment, first-player arrangement and full turn-order procedure belong to broader setup and are not separately requested by this question.

Recall timing and the most-VP victory condition are accurate elaborations supplied by A and B respectively; the question requires that the Rival can trigger Endgame and can win, not a complete endgame resolution procedure.

a.reason: A identifies all requested component types and quantities, differentiates garrison/supply troops and initial/third Agents, gives one water and both zero markers, retains Reshuffle in Hagal, and correctly allows Rival Endgame and victory. Its omission of exact Influence-cube track positions and Spy/water supply locations does not omit a separately requested material fact under the actual wording.
a.exact_response: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes, 3 troops in garrison and 9 in supply, 2 Agents in supply and the third beside the board, 3 Spies, 1 water, and score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor; its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.

b.exact_response: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes, one at the bottom of each Faction track; three troops in its garrison and nine in supply; two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board; three Spies and 1 water in supply; score and Combat markers at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and keep the 2P Reshuffle card in its deck. The Rival can trigger Endgame at 10 or more VP and can win by having the most VP.
